children: As Jawa celebrates his birthday, his journey from a management trainee at Hindustan Unilever to leading HUL and now advising emerging businesses offers a look at nearly four decades of leadership across brands, markets and business transformation

As Rohit Jawa celebrates his birthday today, his career offers a snapshot of nearly four decades spent navigating some of the world's most competitive consumer markets, from starting out as a management trainee at Hindustan Unilever in 1988 to leading the company as its Managing Director and CEO, and now taking his experience into the venture ecosystem.

Jawa's latest chapter began in August 2026, when he joined Bessemer Venture Partners' Operating Advisor Network. In the role, he is set to work with Bessemer's portfolio companies on market entry and growth, business transformation, brand building, go-to-market excellence and building leadership teams across complex, multi-geography organisations.

The appointment comes shortly after Jawa stepped down as MD and CEO of Hindustan Unilever in July 2025, concluding a little over two years at the helm of one of India's largest FMCG businesses. Priya Nair succeeded him as HUL's MD and CEO from August 1, 2025.
From HUL Trainee To Global Unilever Leadership

Jawa's association with Unilever began in 1988, when he joined Hindustan Unilever as a management trainee. Over the course of his career, he went on to hold senior leadership positions across India, China, the Philippines, Singapore and the UK.

Among the defining chapters of his international career was his time as Executive Vice President, North Asia and Chairman of Unilever China. He also served as Chairman and CEO of Unilever Philippines, where he led a business transformation and growth programme.

Before returning to India, Jawa served as Unilever's Global Chief of Transformation. The role placed him at the centre of a major organisational redesign, including changes to P&L accountability and operating structures across the company's global operations. He was also a member of Unilever's Global Executive Committee from 2023 to 2025.
His international experience has been a consistent feature of his career, giving him exposure to different consumer markets, operating models and stages of business transformation.
Returning To Lead HUL
In 2023, Jawa returned to India as President, Unilever South Asia, and CEO and Managing Director of Hindustan Unilever.

At HUL, he led an approximately $7 billion business through portfolio, channel and organisational transformation, with the focus on strengthening competitiveness and preparing the business for its next phase of growth, according to Bessemer.

His tenure came at a time when India's FMCG sector was dealing with evolving consumer preferences, changing channels, premiumisation and a rapidly shifting digital landscape. His leadership agenda included sharpening the portfolio, strengthening the business's competitiveness and continuing HUL's transformation across channels and operations.
Jawa stepped down from the HUL role on July 31, 2025, bringing to a close a career at Unilever that had stretched across more than three decades.
A New Chapter Beyond The Corporate Boardroom

A year after leaving HUL, Jawa's move to Bessemer marks a different kind of leadership role. Instead of leading a single consumer business, he is now working with companies across a portfolio, bringing experience in areas such as market expansion, brand building, go-to-market strategy and organisational transformation.

For the marketing and business community, the transition is notable because of the breadth of experience Jawa brings from Unilever — particularly his exposure to building brands and businesses across multiple markets and navigating organisations through periods of transformation.

His career has also maintained a strong connection with marketing. Before moving into broader business leadership, Jawa held roles spanning sales, operations and marketing, while his later positions placed him at the intersection of brand building, organisational change and business growth.
A Career That Keeps Evolving

Jawa's birthday comes at an interesting point in that journey. After spending much of his professional life inside one of the world's largest consumer companies, he is now applying that experience to businesses at a different stage of their growth.
Bessemer says Jawa will work with its portfolio companies on areas including Asia market entry and growth, business transformation, brand building, go-to-market excellence and leadership development.

That makes his latest move less of a conventional post-corporate transition and more of a continuation of the themes that have defined his career: building businesses, navigating change, developing brands and preparing organisations for their next stage.

As Rohit Jawa celebrates another birthday, his professional journey continues to evolve — from the corridors of Hindustan Unilever to leadership roles across global markets, the HUL boardroom and now the emerging-business ecosystem.

For a leader whose career has spanned nearly four decades, the latest chapter is another shift in setting, but one that remains closely connected to the areas that have defined his work: brands, transformation, markets and people.
